LESSON: SHIRK OF SHIRK SHIRK

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Pillars of Iman
Topic 3.2: Shirk of Shirk Shirk

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Shirk of Shirk Shirk. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should a Muslim avoid shirk?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain different types of shirk to avoid associating Allah with other beings
2. describe different ways through which shirk is manifested to protect one’s Iman
3. practise acts that are devoid of shirk in daily life
4. recognise the belief in One God as the foundation of Iman

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SHIRK OF SHIRK SHIRK
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Shirk of Shirk Shirk helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SHIRK OF SHIRK SHIRK
Study Shirk of Shirk Shirk like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain different types of shirk to avoid associating Allah with other beings

What this means
In this part you learn to explain different types of shirk to avoid associating Allah with other beings. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain different types of shirk to avoid associating Allah with other beings.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Shirk of Shirk Shirk” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain different types of shirk to avoid associating Allah with other beings. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe different ways through which shirk is manifested to protect one’s Iman

What this means
In this part you learn to describe different ways through which shirk is manifested to protect one’s Iman. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe different ways through which shirk is manifested to protect one’s Iman.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Shirk of Shirk Shirk in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe different ways through which shirk is manifested to protect one’s Iman. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise acts that are devoid of shirk in daily life

What this means
In this part you learn to practise acts that are devoid of shirk in daily life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise acts that are devoid of shirk in daily life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise acts that are devoid of shirk in daily life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Recognise the belief in One God as the foundation of Iman

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the belief in One God as the foundation of Iman. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the belief in One God as the foundation of Iman.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Shirk of Shirk Shirk” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the belief in One God as the foundation of Iman. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Shirk of Shirk Shirk is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Shirk of Shirk Shirk” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain different types of shirk to avoid associating Allah with other beings)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Shirk of Shirk Shirk in your own words. (skill: describe different ways through which shirk is manifested to protect one’s Iman)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise acts that are devoid of shirk in daily life)

Example 4: Show how “Shirk of Shirk Shirk” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: recognise the belief in One God as the foundation of Iman)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Shirk of Shirk Shirk to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain different types of shirk to avoid associating Allah with other beings.
3. Practise this skill: describe different ways through which shirk is manifested to protect one’s Iman.
4. Practise this skill: practise acts that are devoid of shirk in daily life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Shirk of Shirk Shirk from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Shirk of Shirk Shirk: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Shirk of Shirk Shirk?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should a Muslim avoid shirk?
2. How can a Muslim avoid shirk?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Shirk of Shirk Shirk means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain different types of shirk to avoid associating Allah with other beings.
5. Be able to: describe different ways through which shirk is manifested to protect one’s Iman.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
